Virginia localities generally lack a general moratorium power, and this action is structured as a deferral of discretionary applications tied to a pending comprehensive plan amendment rather than an outright application freeze, consistent with the state note on Virginia's narrow local authority. Three other events tagged 'Moratorium vote' in the same chronology sweep were reviewed and rejected as candidates: Suffolk (2026-06-17) only directed the Planning Commission to draft a permanent citywide prohibition, with no numbered instrument enacted; Front Royal (2026-06-23) rejected an enabling zoning amendment and directed staff to prepare moratorium language within 60 days, again with no enacted ordinance located; Loudoun County (2026-07-22) explicitly directed staff only to research the legality and scope of a possible pause, with the chronology stating no moratorium or processing pause was enacted by that vote.
